name: shell
description: Run a command with bash, stdout and stderr together. The result's first line is [exit N], or [killed] if it was stopped; the output follows. Output over 100000 bytes is not shown: the first line says how many bytes and lines it has, and the file it is in, for you to read parts of with head, tail, sed -n, grep or awk. When a command succeeds and prints a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image (cat shot.png), you see the image, if it is 3000000 bytes or less; send stderr elsewhere for those, or its messages corrupt the image. Other output that is not text is not shown. Each call is a fresh shell in the working directory. You get the result when the command ends, unless wait runs out or a message arrives first: then it goes on as a job, and its result arrives later as a message of its own.

command.description: The command line, as you would type it.

wait.description: Seconds to wait before it goes on as a job; 0 for a server or anything you need not wait for. By default, until it ends.
